feature: Harden the paper: feedback loops, discoverability, and the screens still on paper only
notes: Every story here must be completable in one context window. If one turns out not to be, split it in prd.json and say so in progress.txt rather than half-finishing it.
Stories carrying blockedBy need something from a human. Skip them; never clear the field yourself.

userStories.title: Move the check suites into the repository
userStories.why: Ten numeric check suites exist and are the project's core verification discipline, but they live in a temporary scratchpad outside the repo. A fresh agent — which is every Ralph iteration — has none of them. Until this lands there is no feedback loop and broken code compounds silently.
acceptanceCriteria: All ten suites live in checks/ in the repository
Their absolute file:///C:/Users/... imports become relative, so they run on any machine and on a CI runner
npm run check runs every suite and exits non-zero if any fails
Running npm run check on a clean tree passes
Deliberately breaking one thing each suite guards makes that suite fail, and this is demonstrated rather than assumed

userStories.title: Run the checks in GitHub Actions
userStories.why: The nightly press run rebuilds the edition and can move any figure the suites assert on. Nobody reads a green log, but everybody notices a red one.
acceptanceCriteria: A workflow runs npx tsc --noEmit, npm run check and npm run build on push and pull request
It does not run the ingestion, the model or the recorder — those cost time and quota and are the press run's job
The edition workflow also runs the checks after it commits, so a bad edition is visible the morning it lands
The workflow is verified by reading a real run, not by reasoning about the YAML

userStories.title: Let the index search every edition, not just today
userStories.why: 237 stories are reachable and permanently addressed, but app/search/page.tsx calls getDigest(), so only today's 54 are findable. 183 columns are reachable and undiscoverable from inside the paper.
acceptanceCriteria: Search covers the whole archive through lib/archive.ts
A result says which edition it was printed in, using the dateline vocabulary already in lib/digest.ts
Today's paper outranks an older printing of the same event
The cost of searching 237 and growing is considered and the trade-off stated in a comment
A check asserts an archive-only story is findable by its headline
Verified in the browser: search a term that appears only in an archived story and see it

userStories.title: Generate the Open Graph card images
userStories.why: Every page declares twitter:card=summary_large_image and supplies no image, which is the weakest possible state: the card reserves a large slot and shows nothing. A shared story should unfurl as a clipping from this paper.
acceptanceCriteria: Uses Next's opengraph-image file convention; app/sitemap.ts and the per-page openGraph blocks deliberately left images unset for this
A root card and a per-story card at minimum
The real typefaces render, not a fallback sans — ImageResponse does not inherit next/font, so the font data has to be supplied and the licence checked
Build time is reported before and after; if it becomes unacceptable, say so with numbers rather than quietly reducing scope
The built HTML emits og:image with absolute URLs resolved from metadataBase
The generated images are looked at, not merely generated

userStories.title: Give the index and Your Edition their own share cards
userStories.why: Both inherit the root openGraph block, so a shared link to either reads 'The AI Daily — Two Cents Edition' rather than what the page is. Small, and the last gap in the metadata work.
acceptanceCriteria: app/search/page.tsx and app/yours/page.tsx declare their own openGraph and twitter blocks
siteName and locale are restated, because Next replaces the parent block rather than merging into it
No openGraph.images is set if og-images has not landed yet
Verified by reading the built HTML for both routes

userStories.title: Make the briefing's pacing drift impossible to miss
userStories.why: The recorder warns when a take is more than 4% off its prediction. It fired on the press run of 2026-09-19 and nobody read the log, so the bulletin was billed at five minutes and ran 4:37 for two days. A warning nobody reads is not a feedback loop.
acceptanceCriteria: The recorder writes the predicted seconds into public/briefing/manifest.json alongside the measured ones
A check asserts the committed manifest's drift is inside tolerance, so npm run check catches it without anyone reading a log
The field is optional on read, exactly as script is, so a manifest written before this lands is still playable
Demonstrated to fail on a manifest with an out-of-tolerance drift

userStories.title: Switch on generated copy in the bulletin
userStories.why: lib/briefing.ts already accepts generated copy and app/briefing/page.tsx already has the comment describing the one-line change. It is off because the page and the recorder must pass the identical fourth argument — one without the other desynchronises the marks from the script.
acceptanceCriteria: app/briefing/page.tsx and services/ai/voice.ts both pass the brief lookup, in the same change
The script fingerprint matches between page and manifest afterwards, verified with the real recording
Anything a model wrote carries a visible label, which is the paper's standing rule
The bulletin is re-recorded and the take is inside tolerance
userStories.blockedBy: No working model provider key. Needs GROQ_API_KEY as a repository secret before any generated copy exists to switch on.

userStories.title: Build the subscription screen from the approved mockup
userStories.why: The account panel exists but is a plain form. The approved design sets it as a period order coupon on glass — underlines rather than boxes, delivery hour as a real choice, the price stated plainly, and nothing demanded before the paper has been read.
acceptanceCriteria: Matches screen 05 of the approved mockup in scripts/ralph/mockups/ if present, otherwise the design described in UI-GUIDE.md
Uses the .glass class rather than declaring backdrop-filter, which is suspended during page turns for a measured reason
Readable in both editions and at phone width
No credential is collected that the project cannot yet store — accounts are dormant until Firebase is configured
Verified in the browser at phone and desktop width

userStories.title: Turn the dormant accounts on
userStories.why: Account code is written and wired but inert. It needs a Firebase project's public config and firestore.rules deployed.
acceptanceCriteria: NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* values configured
firestore.rules deployed
Sign-in, registration and preference sync verified end to end in the browser
userStories.blockedBy: Needs the owner's Firebase project config. The NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are not secrets and can be pasted in chat.

userStories.title: Run the paper on a real handset
userStories.why: Never once run on a phone. The grain tiling, the installed icon and splash, the offline round-trip and the page turn under a real finger are all unverified on hardware.
acceptanceCriteria: The app loads on a physical device
The corner peel is dragged by hand and the spine holds
Grain, icon, splash and offline behaviour are each confirmed or reported broken
userStories.blockedBy: Needs a physical phone or an emulator. LAN was blocked by router AP isolation; expo tunnel is the known workaround.
